messages.text: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat

metadata.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for rule changes to Formula 1 Virtual Safety Car rules after losing out on win to Kimi Antonelli | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for rule changes to Formula 1 Virtual Safety Car rules after losing out on win to Kimi Antonelli Lando Norris says the timing of the Virtual Safety Car at the Spanish Grand Prix was "unfair" as it cost him victory to Kimi Antonelli in Madrid; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 13 September 2026 18:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris admits team 'were too quick' after missing a crucial VSC pit stop that cost him race lead Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix. Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions. However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track. messages.text: Dominant Lowry storms to record 11-stroke triumph at Irish Open

metadata.summary: Shane Lowry stormed to a record 11-shot victory at the Amgen Irish Open, the home crowd favourite shooting a seven-under 63 on Sunday to finish a staggering 23 under par.
metadata.content: Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry secures record 11-stroke victory at Trump International Links in Doonbeg | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Amgen Irish Open: Shane Lowry secures record 11-stroke victory at Trump International Links in Doonbeg Shane Lowry cards eight birdies in final-round 63, including one at the 18th to sign off his stunning triumph in style; Rory McIlory defiant, saying "I don't feel too far away" after signing off disappointing title defence with a round of 67 to finish one under Sunday 13 September 2026 19:31, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the Amgen Irish Open. Shane Lowry stormed to a record 11-shot victory at the Amgen Irish Open, the home crowd favourite shooting a seven-under 63 on Sunday to finish a staggering 23 under par. It's Lowry's seventh career title and his second Irish Open triumph, following his 2009 victory as a 22-year-old amateur, with US President Donald Trump presenting him with the trophy. It's a welcome return to the winner's circle for Lowry after a series of agonising near-misses earlier this season, including a double-bogey on the final hole that cost him the Dubai Invitational by two strokes and a collapse at the Cognizant Classic, where he surrendered a three-stroke lead with three holes to play by closing with two double-bogeys. Europe regained the trophy after an exciting final day at a rainy Bernardus Golf, where Nordqvist's side won seven of the 12 points available to claim a 15-13 win over Team USA. The visitors felt they had 'turned the tide' in their favour after a sensational finish the previous evening, where Jennifer Kupcho's sensational late birdies levelled the biennial contest, but Europe bounced back to earn a first outright win since 2021.
